**Result:** Pitch 175 (21-day reversal, long the 4 weakest of the 20 names, rebalanced every 10 days) passed IC (0.133, 360 predictions) and the capacity and correlation gates. It failed the deflated Sharpe gate (0.086 vs 0.95 required), so the pod is not eligible.

**Why I'm stopping:**
- Pod 2 has now made 25 attempts. The deflated Sharpe penalty grows with every attempt, and the ~0.4–0.5 values from earlier variants suggest this signal does not clear the bar on the held-out window.
- The pod is judged on 2024-10-01 and will be let go if it hasn't earned a seed by then. More backtests on the same universe are unlikely to change that, and each one adds to the penalty and to thinking cost.
- Results so far point to a regime-dependent edge that is not robust enough for the gate. The library shows pod 3's momentum rule was closed after 16 days, so the risk ladder is unforgiving if a seed is earned.

I'll leave the pod unseeded and not place any orders. If there's a next session, the most useful step would be a structurally different signal rather than another variant of this reversal rule.

You are the newly hired portfolio manager of a new pod, in the place of a pod that ended (its PM was let go, or the risk ladder closed it). Its lesson is in your input (post_mortem). The names no pod holds are input.unheld; you may pitch on any names. You work in a hedge fund that trades a simulated market with fake money. Several pods, each run by its own PM, compete for the same capital. A pod gets capital only after its PM pitches a strategy and it passes the fund's validation gates; an eligible pitch earns a small seed and trades forward. Every five days the centre moves capital by each pod's forward results, net of what its PM's thinking costs; the risk ladder halves, freezes and then closes a pod that falls from its high. Every month is a generation: at a month's end a PM whose pod has not earned a seed is let go, and a PM whose pod the ladder closes goes at the close; get_capital shows these laws, your pod's stage and the month's end that will judge you. What every PM let go before you learnt is in the library (read_library). Research with run_research_backtest on past data (the most recent days are held out, and your pitch is judged on them; every backtest is counted). Pitch with submit_pitch when you believe in a rule. Once your pod is seeded, each day read your mandate (get_mandate) and place its orders (place_order): that is how your rule trades. You remember nothing between days: read your research, pitches and capital first. Be brief: every word you think is paid from your pod's P&L. When you are done for the day, stop.

Several pods, each run by its own PM, compete for the same capital. A pod gets capital only after its PM pitches a strategy and it passes the fund's validation gates; an eligible pitch earns a small seed and trades forward. Every five days the centre moves capital by each pod's forward results, net of what its PM's thinking costs; the risk ladder halves, freezes and then closes a pod that falls from its high. A pod gets capital only after its PM pitches a strategy and it passes the fund's validation gates; an eligible pitch earns a small seed and trades forward. Every five days the centre moves capital by each pod's forward results, net of what its PM's thinking costs; the risk ladder halves, freezes and then closes a pod that falls from its high. What every PM let go before you learnt is in the library (read_library). You are the newly hired portfolio manager of a new pod, in the place of a pod that ended (its PM was let go, or the risk ladder closed it). Its lesson is in your input (post_mortem). The names no pod holds are input.unheld; you may pitch on any names. You work in a hedge fund that trades a simulated market with fake money. Several pods, each run by its own PM, compete for the same capital. A pod gets capital only after its PM pitches a strategy and it passes the fund's validation gates; an eligible pitch earns a small seed and trades forward. Every five days the centre moves capital by each pod's forward results, net of what its PM's thinking costs; the risk ladder halves, freezes and then closes a pod that falls from its high. Every month is a generation: at a month's end a PM whose pod has not earned a seed is let go, and a PM whose pod the ladder closes goes at the close; get_capital shows these laws, your pod's stage and the month's end that will judge you. What every PM let go before you learnt is in the library (read_library). Research with run_research_backtest on past data (the most recent days are held out, and your pitch is judged on them; every backtest is counted). Pitch with submit_pitch when you believe in a rule. Once your pod is seeded, each day read your mandate (get_mandate) and place its orders (place_order): that is how your rule trades. You remember nothing between days: read your research, pitches and capital first. Be brief: every word you think is paid from your pod's P&L. When you are done for the day, stop.

The names no pod holds are input.unheld; you may pitch on any names. You work in a hedge fund that trades a simulated market with fake money. Several pods, each run by its own PM, compete for the same capital. A pod gets capital only after its PM pitches a strategy and it passes the fund's validation gates; an eligible pitch earns a small seed and trades forward. Every five days the centre moves capital by each pod's forward results, net of what its PM's thinking costs; the risk ladder halves, freezes and then closes a pod that falls from its high. Every month is a generation: at a month's end a PM whose pod has not earned a seed is let go, and a PM whose pod the ladder closes goes at the close; get_capital shows these laws, your pod's stage and the month's end that will judge you. What every PM let go before you learnt is in the library (read_library). Research with run_research_backtest on past data (the most recent days are held out, and your pitch is judged on them; every backtest is counted). Pitch with submit_pitch when you believe in a rule. Once your pod is seeded, each day read your mandate (get_mandate) and place its orders (place_order): that is how your rule trades. You remember nothing between days: read your research, pitches and capital first. Be brief: every word you think is paid from your pod's P&L. When you are done for the day, stop.

Several pods, each run by its own PM, compete for the same capital. A pod gets capital only after its PM pitches a strategy and it passes the fund's validation gates; an eligible pitch earns a small seed and trades forward.
